subject: Re: Evergreen Analytics — renewal term tweak & capacity bundle review
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura@evergreen.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Devon Park <devon.park@evergreen.ai>, Procurement <procurement@evergreen.ai>
Date: 2026-04-27T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Evergreen renewal request: term tweak + capacity bundle (order bundle v3 attached)

Hi Grace,

Hope you’re well — we’re preparing Evergreen’s renewal packet and want to propose a slightly different commercial structure that would help with predictability across projects. In short: could we shift our 12-month term to a 15-month alignment window (Mar 1–May 31 crossover) and add a capacity bundle of 1.2M token units (billed as a committed add-on) to start on the renewal date?

Attached is our current PO and a draft order bundle (Evergreen_OrderBundle_v3.docx) with the SKU layout. Procurement is asking for a Redline-ready MSA and order form this week — they need final paperwork to route for signature by May 10. Can your team confirm:
- whether a 15-month term is acceptable and whether proration will apply for the partial first/last month;
- if committed bundle billing will be monthly or front-loaded; and
- whether Redwood can agree to the requested data-retention language (see paragraph 6) or provide an alternate we can circulate.

Thanks — I can jump on a quick call if that’s easier.

Laura Chen
Head of Cloud Operations
Evergreen Analytics

[Attachment: Evergreen_OrderBundle_v3.docx (docx)]
[Attachment: PO_45521.pdf (pdf)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-27T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Evergreen renewal request: term tweak + capacity bundle (order bundle v3 attached)

Marissa / Markus — forwarding Evergreen's ask. Quick summary: Evergreen wants term shifted to 15 months and a committed 1.2M token bundle on renewal, PO attached. Procurement has a May 10 deadline for signature routing.

Proposed next steps:
1) Markus — please review the attached MSA redline request and call out any non-starters (data retention, SLA credit language, liability cap interaction with committed-bundle credits).
2) Marissa — do we have flexibility on billing cadence for committed bundles (monthly amortized vs upfront)? Also need your input on commercial sequencing (PO first vs DocuSign).
3) Mateo — once legal signs off, please prepare an updated order form and create a DocuSign powerform link; Evergreen has limited time.

If this is doable within 3 business days we can meet the May 10 procurement window. I’ll loop back with a short doc summarizing our positions for Evergreen.

Thanks — Grace
Account Executive, Renewals
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-27T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Evergreen renewal request: term tweak + capacity bundle (order bundle v3 attached)

Grace / Marissa — I reviewed the attachments and prepared an annotated redline. High-level flags:

1) Data retention (para 6) — Evergreen's requested retention window and right to request raw logs is broader than our standard. We can offer a 13-month retention for production logs and propose a separate SOW for extended retention with pricing.

2) SLA / credit stack — their requested credit waterfall interacts poorly with committed-bundle billing. If a credit applies against committed consumption, we need explicit language to avoid double-crediting and to clarify the billing period impacted.

3) Term/proration — shifting to 15 months is commercially fine, but proration language must be explicit: prorate the first partial period at the renewal effective date; thereafter, standard monthly invoicing. We should avoid ambiguous wording about ‘pro-rata refunds’.

4) Exhibit A / model variants — Evergreen wants a fallback to a CPU-quantized variant as a resilience option. We need to capture performance SLAs for fallback variants or exclude them from SLA credits.

I attached: Redline_MSA_v2-markus.docx with tracked changes and comments. My ask: Grace/Marissa, confirm whether we can require the extended-retention to be a billable add-on and whether sales want to accept a monthly amortized committed-bundle (which reduces cash collected up front but eases procurement). If sales prefer upfront billing, call that out and I’ll tighten the credit/proration language accordingly.

Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Redline_MSA_v2-markus.docx (docx)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura@evergreen.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-28T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evergreen renewal request: term tweak + capacity bundle (order bundle v3 attached)

Laura — thanks for the packet and for the clear ask. A few commercial clarifications to speed routing:
- Billing cadence: Redwood can offer the committed 1.2M token bundle either as (A) upfront prepaid for the 15-month term, or (B) monthly amortized billing across the 15 months. Upfront gives Evergreen a 1.5% prepayment discount; monthly amortization is cash-flow neutral but will start immediate monthly invoicing. Which does procurement prefer?
- Proration: we’ll prorate the first partial month of the new 15-month term (explicitly on a per-day basis) — that’s standard.
- PO vs DocuSign: procurement can send a signed PO (we’ll accept) but we ask that the MSA + order form be executed via DocuSign for auditability. We can sequence PO receipt -> DocuSign send once legal confirms redlines.

Next steps:
1) Markus to finalize redline (Grace / Markus, are the flags above accurate?).
2) If Evergreen confirms billing preference (prepay vs amortize), I’ll prepare two order form numbers and a DocuSign package.
3) Suggest a quick 30-min alignment call tomorrow (Apr 29) to close commercial terms and confirm legal positions.

Laura, can you confirm procurement’s preference on billing? If they want the upfront discount we’ll add that to the order form and adjust the DocuSign bundle.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Enterprise Renewals
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Chen <laura@evergreen.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@evergreen.ai>, Devon Park <devon.park@evergreen.ai>
Date: 2026-04-30T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evergreen renewal request: term tweak + capacity bundle (order bundle v3 attached)

Thanks team — quick responses below and a signed PO attached.

- Procurement prefers the monthly amortized billing for the committed bundle (cashflow reasons).
- The 15-month term and proration model you described are acceptable. Please include the per-day proration formula in the order form.
- On data retention: Evergreen would like a 24-month retention for audit logs; we understand that’s beyond standard. If Redwood can offer 13 months as standard and provide a priced option for 24 months we can accept that path.

We’re ready to proceed: attached is the signed PO (Evergreen_PO_signed_45521.pdf). Please send the redline MSA back to us via DocuSign once you’ve incorporated Markus’ comments. Procurement is aiming to sign the final DocuSign envelope by May 8.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. I’m available for a 30-min call tomorrow (Apr 30) after 11am PT if helpful.

Laura Chen
Head of Cloud Operations
Evergreen Analytics

[Attachment: Evergreen_PO_signed_45521.pdf (pdf)]
